note: Compares open source and proprietary medical models and the metrics used to judge them.
title: Large language models in healthcare and medical domain: A review

reading.body:
This review compares open-source and proprietary medical language models directly, alongside the metrics researchers use to judge them.

Comparing the two directly is useful because open-source and proprietary medical models face different practical constraints. An open-source model can be run entirely within a hospital's own infrastructure, which matters for data privacy, while a proprietary model may offer stronger raw performance but requires sending patient data to an external vendor.

The review does not recommend one category over the other, and does not report deployment cost or the compute infrastructure required to run the open-source options it discusses.

explain_beginner: This paper surveys how advanced AI language models are being used in healthcare. These models can read and understand medical questions and information remarkably well. The researchers reviewed what these models can do, from identifying medical terms in documents to answering patient questions, and compared different models available to hospitals and clinics. They also explained the measurements used to determine whether these models work properly and identified obstacles that still need solving before widespread use.
explain_business: Healthcare organizations considering LLM deployment should understand that these systems can meaningfully improve clinical documentation processing and information retrieval. This review enables decision-makers to evaluate available options by comparing proprietary versus open-source models and understanding how to measure their performance. However, organizations should recognize significant limitations and constraints remain. The findings indicate LLMs offer genuine efficiency potential in healthcare operations but require careful assessment of specific use cases and ongoing research before large-scale implementation.
explain_practitioner: This comprehensive review examines LLM applications across healthcare tasks including named entity recognition, relation extraction, natural language inference, multimodal analysis, document classification, and question-answering. The authors trace development from traditional pretrained language models through current LLMs, evaluate state-of-the-art proprietary and open-source models, and detail performance metrics for biomedical evaluation. The work synthesizes existing healthcare LLM functionalities, assesses comparative effectiveness across implementations, and identifies technical limitations and implementation challenges requiring further research and development.
